chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sahl ibn al-Yasa', from his father who said:
I asked Abu Al-Hassan (peace be upon him) about the woman who dyes (her hair) while she is menstruating. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with it'.

key_terms.تَخْتَضِبُ: She dyes (specifically hair with henna or similar)
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: There is no problem with it / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a menstruating woman to dye her hair?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) clarifies that the ritual impurity (*hadath*) of menstruation does not restrict a woman from engaging in personal adornment, such as dyeing her hair. This ruling highlights the distinction between states requiring prayer abstention and those permitting general daily activities, reflecting the practical flexibility in Shia jurisprudence regarding women's hygiene and beauty during their cycle.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Sahl Bin Al Yas’a, from his father who said,
‘I asked Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> about the woman dyeing (her hair) and she is menstruating. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no prolem with it’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Sahl ibn al-Yasa’ from his father who has said the following: “
I once asked abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a woman who uses dye during her Hayd (menses). He (the Imam) said, ’It is not harmful.”’
